content.comment_body: I have a [product_name] with transistor outputs ([article_no]). The documentation states that these outputs are protected against overload and short circuit. Today, an output was overloaded with 600 mA, while the manual specifies a maximum of 300 mA. Now, the transistor output is damaged and remains switched on regardless of control signals. It appears that the protection for the transistor output did not function. Has anyone else encountered this issue?
From my perspective, you should reach out to [company_name] directly for support. Starting a support request would be advisable in your situation.

It seems like the output transistor has failed. Repair might be needed. The root cause seems to be the overload on the PLC output; even replacing the PLC may result in the same issue if the cause persists. I recommend using a relay at the output to handle the higher current. If this is affecting production, you can use a spare output, activate a relay from that, and connect your load via the relay. Hope this helps.

I have also reported this problem to [company_name]. I was hoping to find someone with prior experience with this issue. I tried moving the output to another channel, but it failed just as quickly as the first. I've now changed the control setup so the output has less load, but before that, I unfortunately need a new [product_name]. I used a [article_no], which once failed because of a transistor output, though this time the [product_name] did not break.

analysis.insight_summary: A user experienced a transistor output failure on a [product_name] after exceeding the recommended current limit. The built-in overload and short-circuit protections described in the manual did not prevent hardware damage, resulting in an output stuck in the 'on' state. Attempts to use alternative outputs caused similar failures, suggesting a broader issue with the protective mechanisms. The user perceives the protection features as insufficient, leading to repeated equipment damage.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the hardware's automatic overload and short-circuit protection to operate as described in the handbook and to reliably prevent device damage, even if an accidental overload occurs.
